# Underlying values

Setup

``` r

library(Spectran)
library(gt)
library(dplyr)
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'dplyr'
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':
#> 
#>     filter, lag
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
#> 
#>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union
library(purrr)
library(tidyr)

table_fun <- function(data) {   
  data %>% gt() %>% 
  tab_style(
    style = cell_borders(
      sides = c("left", "right"),
      color = "grey"),
    locations = list(
      cells_body(
      columns = everything()
      ),
      cells_column_labels()
    )
    )
}
  
```

## Preface

This document describes and summarizes the various values that are used
by Spectran. Because the tables are comprehensive, it makes little sense
to go through them sequentially. Instead, you can use the table of
contents to jump to the section of interest.

## Action Spectra

The units in the following tables are nm (nanometers) for wavelength,
and 1 for the action spectrum. The action spectrum is a relative
measure, and therefore has no unit. The data for alpha-opic action
spectra were taken from the [CIE S026
Toolbox](https://cie.co.at/publications/cie-system-metrology-optical-radiation-iprgc-influenced-responses-light-0).
The 2° photopic luminous efficiency function V(λ) (between 380-780 nm)
was taken from the [ISO/CIE
23539:2023](https://cie.co.at/publications/photometry-cie-system-physical-photometry-3).

``` r

Specs$AS_wide %>% rename(Wavelength = Wellenlaenge) %>% table_fun()
```

## Efficacy of luminous radiation

The values for alpha-opic quantities were taken from the [CIE S026
Toolbox](https://cie.co.at/publications/cie-system-metrology-optical-radiation-iprgc-influenced-responses-light-0).
The 2° photopic luminous efficiency function V(λ) (between 380-780 nm)
was taken from the [ISO/CIE
23539:2023](https://cie.co.at/publications/photometry-cie-system-physical-photometry-3).

Efficacy

``` r

Efficacy <- Specs$Efficacy %>% 
  as_tibble() %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), values_to = "inverse Efficacy") %>% 
  mutate(Efficacy = 1/`inverse Efficacy`*1000) %>% table_fun() %>% 
  tab_footnote(footnote = "lm/W",locations = cells_column_labels(
    columns = "inverse Efficacy")) %>% 
  tab_footnote(footnote = "mW/lm",locations = cells_column_labels(
    columns = "Efficacy")) %>% 
  tab_options(footnotes.multiline = FALSE) %>% 
  fmt_number(drop_trailing_zeros = TRUE, decimals = 7, sep_mark = " ")
```

``` r

Efficacy
```

For plotting and table creation, Peak wavelengths, colors, an
abbreviations were used. These can be found in the following table.

``` r

Specs$Plot %>% table_fun() %>%   tab_footnote(footnote = "Wavelength (nm)",locations = cells_column_labels(

  data_color(columns = Col, fn = \(x) Specs$Plot$Col)
```

``` r
  tibble(`Wavelength (nm)` = names(.),
```
